title: Ordinary module pullback oplax mate on balanced generators
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and take their small pro-étale sites small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], also writing $R_T$ for its reconstructed section-ring sheaf. Let $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the fixed equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary module operations, their specified adjunctions, and geometric composition comparisons of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Use relative tensors [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] internally and sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] externally, identified by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Give internal pullback its actual oplax structure induced by the abelian inverse-image mate structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and extension of scalars [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. For all internal $R_Y$-module objects $M,N$, under $E_X,E_Y$ the ordinary oplax tensor arrow is the normalized ringed comparison [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]. Writing $S=R_X$, $R'=f^{-1}R_Y$, it sends $s\otimes(m\otimes n)$ to $(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$ from $S\otimes_{R'}f^{-1}(M\otimes_{R_Y}N)$ to $(S\otimes_{R'}f^{-1}M)\otimes_S(S\otimes_{R'}f^{-1}N)$. Its inverse sends $(s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n)$ to $st\otimes(m\otimes n)$. The unit comparison is scalar multiplication, and these formulas respect the associators and unitors.

proof.text: Use the fixed pure-tensor comparison and its uniqueness to obtain naturality of ordinaryTensorComparison. Apply internal_direct_image_lax_realization for compatibility of adjunction units, right-adjoint tensor pairing, and right-adjoint unit. Apply composite_module_oplax_mate for the internal tensor and unit mate equations. A direct calculation with the two adjunction Hom equivalences transports these equations: naturality of the right-adjoint comparison and the compatible units transport every mate, and tensor naturality then identifies the section tensor and unit maps.

For the actual internal tensor map, use the already proved upperStar_tensorπ_delta in ProEtaleSectionModuleFunctors. Precompose with the ambient inverse-image tensor constraint, cancel its inverse constraint, and use naturality of the balanced tensor projection. The coefficient pullback map is an isomorphism, and the inverse of extendScalarsIsoComapInv on underlying sheaves is extendUnitHom. Evaluation on m tensor n proves the formula with both scalars equal to one.

In a general abelian sheaf-module category, whiskerLeft_extendUnitHom_smul identifies the scalar-extension generator with scalar multiplication on the inserted section. The internal-section tensor isomorphism is injective on sections and carries pure tensors to pure tensors; hence internal pure tensors satisfy (s m) tensor (t n) = st (m tensor n), by the usual TensorProduct identity and linearity of sheafification. Apply the inverse tensor map to the inserted formula and use delta followed by mu equal to identity. These identities and linearity give the inverse scalar formula. The inverse map is injective because mu followed by delta is identity, so cancelling it and using the inverse formula with t=1 gives the forward scalar formula. The unit formula is the existing extendUnitHom_eta_upperStar identity followed by linearity.
Apply the associativity, left_unitality_hom, and right_unitality_hom laws of the specified section pullback oplax monoidal structure. These give exactly the three final constraint equations.
